reportOnlyUntil: REPORT ONLY until a steward dispatches it. This file routes nothing by existing; the lane writes only under BACKFILL_APPLY=true. Dispatch SCOPE=data/pool-relocations/<this file>, one part at a time.
finding: 16,125 baseball pool rows sit on `bowman-paper`, which holds ZERO checklist-backed catalog rows in EVERY year measured, while `bowman` is fully checklist-backed in every one. A row left on `bowman-paper` can never match anything.
rulings: THIS IS A FOLD, NOT A RUNG-MEMBERSHIP MOVE. R39 moved only rows whose stated rung proved they belonged to a sibling PRODUCT. R44 is about the KEY itself: `bowman-paper` is an alias, not a product, so every row on it belongs on `bowman` whatever its rung. No rung test is applied and none would be meaningful.

NOTHING IS TAKEN FROM A CHECKLIST THAT NAMES IT. `bowman-paper` holds 0 checklist-backed rows in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — measured, not assumed — so no card loses an address a source gave it.

A FOLD IS NOT A LICENCE TO SKIP THE GUARDS. A destination year with no checklist backing is skipped, and split-identity rows (cardId disagreeing with hobbyiqCardId on sport or year) are left for their own lane. Both are counted in `leftAlone`.

TWO SHAPES, as in R34/R35/R39/R41: slug cardId -> RELOCATE (the setKey is in the partition key, so the row really moves); opaque vendor cardId -> REPOINT (hobbyiqCardId patched in place, #1941 address guard runs).
